chapter: Sam Morgan, repertoire and Silver Leaf
title: Manuel Ridgley and the Pelican dance hall
summary: He played upstairs at the Pelican, run by Manuel Ridgley, with the Silver Leaf and Nola bands; Royal Garden and Astoria nearby.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you know Manuel Ridley? Yeah, Manuel Ridley, yeah, I know him.

His brother was, Will Ridley was a trombone player. Manuel Ridley was running a business for Farbacher at Rand Fortin Common. You played that there? Yeah, I played up there on the sort of a dance hall upstairs. Oh yeah? Over there. I played there quite often.
Well I played up there with the Silver Leaf Band, and I played up there with the Nola Band, two on the last. What was the name of the place? I'm trying to think of the name of the place. I see.
Well where was the Royal Guard?
Across the street, opposite this place that we're talking about, was Rand Fortin Common. Up there, the end of-
Well they had the Astoria and the Pelican, and what else along in there?

I don't know, Astoria, Pelican. Well, I'll tell you the truth of people. The Band dollars? I mean the Pelican was what we talking about. Oh, the Pelican. The Pelican was Mario Ridgely. Oh I see. Yeah.

And the other one was the Royal Guard, and they had Astoria. Did you play a long time at the Pelican? Not too long, you know, a couple of months maybe. Were there just a six piece band? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. You don't have any business cards left from those days.
